claims.explanation: Triptolide covalently inhibits XPB/ERCC3, a TFIIH subunit required for RNA polymerase II transcription and nucleotide excision repair, causing rapid RNAPII degradation and transcription arrest. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on high transcriptional output and intact DNA-repair/transcription-coupled repair capacity, so tumors with high ERCC3/XPB expression and functional NER are most sensitive, while those with low XPB, high drug efflux, or apoptosis resistance survive. TP53 loss is common in both groups and is not discriminating; the strongest predictors are ERCC3 expression and NER pathway activity.

features.basis: XPB/ERCC3 is the direct covalent target of triptolide; higher target expression increases drug binding and transcription inhibition
Triptolide arrests RNAPII; high POLR2A expression marks transcriptional addiction and greater sensitivity
NER pathway activity is required for TFIIH function; intact NER correlates with triptolide-induced transcription arrest
XPD is a TFIIH subunit; high expression supports the TFIIH complex targeted by triptolide
Triptolide inhibits NF-kB via RELA; high RELA/NF-kB activity may select for lines that survive through alternative survival signaling
Anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 overexpression confers resistance to apoptosis induced by transcription inhibition
Mcl-1 is a key anti-apoptotic resistance factor against apoptosis-inducing anticancer therapies
Loss-of-function caspase mutations impair apoptosis execution and reduce sensitivity to transcription-inhibitor-induced death
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines but may blunt apoptotic response to transcription stress
Heat shock protein signaling is a resistance mechanism against apoptosis-inducing therapies
Proteasome pathway activity contributes to apoptosis resistance and may protect from triptolide-induced proteotoxic stress
Aberrant nuclear export signaling is a resistance mechanism in apoptosis-resistant cancers
